holes_found.description: Reader-confusion trap: our text cites the dome's prediction-ID 'W015' (lunar magnetic, -1.0 nT) in both detail_evidence and detail_verdict_text. Per raw-text/03-predictions.txt:70 the dome's W015 maps to the dome's WIN-039 — so the citation is ACCURATE. advocate_mode.best_defense: The magnetic-perturbation sign is a reference-frame / component convention. Tyler/Sabaka report a particular vector component (radial) at satellite altitude; the dome's W015 '-1.0 nT' could be quoting a different component or sign convention (e.g., field-decrease at the surface vs enhancement aloft). Under that reading, both describe a ~1 nT lunar-phase modulation and the 'wrong sign' is an artifact of comparing unlike quantities, not a real contradiction.

quantitative_verification.computations: Sign: dome tolerance band [-1.5,-0.5] nT is DISJOINT from observed [+1,+2] nT and opposite in sign — the self-contradiction is verified directly from raw-text/03-predictions.txt:70. Magnitude: a crude order-of-magnitude mu0*sigma*v*B*depth/2 with sigma=3.5 S/m, v=0.5 m/s, B=4e-5 T, depth=4000 m gives ~176 nT — an OVERESTIMATE because it omits satellite-altitude attenuation and the small induced/inducing field ratio; it confirms only that the mechanism produces a detectable-order signal, not the precise 1-2 nT. The authoritative 1-2 nT value rests on Tyler 2003 / Sabaka 2015, cited correctly.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author is right that a real ~1-2 nT lunar-phase geomagnetic signal exists — the empirical phenomenon is genuine, detected by CHAMP and Swarm (wins.json:WIN-039.detail_evidence, citing Tyler 2003 Science 299:239 and Sabaka 2015 doi:10.1002/2015JB012629). kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The dome's own prediction file (raw-text/03-predictions.txt:70) records W015 as -1.0 nT +/-0.5, a negative excursion whose tolerance band [-1.5,-0.5] nT is disjoint from the observed positive +1-2 nT — by the dome's own arithmetic this is not a confirmation (wins.json:WIN-039.detail_evidence). No path from dome geometry (moon altitude 2,534 km) yields 1-2 nT; the magnitude is borrowed from Tyler 2003 (wins.json:WIN-039.detail_verdict_text). The signal-exists kernel cannot survive the dome's self-contradiction in sign plus the post-hoc failure (Part 3.1b, cited in detail_verdict_text).
